description: Run commands using arguments derived from standard input.
A Rust implementation of GNU xargs.

option.name: --arg-file
tip: Read arguments from the given file instead of stdin.

option.name: --delimiter
tip: Use the given delimiter to split the input.

option.name: --exit
tip: Terminate if a constructed command line would exceed the size limit (see -s) rather than reducing the argument count.

option.name: --max-args
tip: Set the max number of arguments read from stdin to be passed to each command invocation (mutually exclusive with -L and -I/-i).

option.name: --max-chars
tip: Set the max number of characters to be passed to each invocation.

option.name: --max-lines
tip: Set the max number of lines from stdin to be passed to each command invocation (mutually exclusive with -n and -I/-i).

option.name: --max-procs
tip: Run up to this many commands in parallel [NOT IMPLEMENTED].

option.name: --no-run-if-empty
tip: If there are no input arguments, do not run the command at all.

option.name: --null
tip: Split the input by null terminators rather than whitespace.

option.name: --replace
tip: If R is specified, the same as -I R; otherwise, the same as -I {}.

option.name: --verbose
tip: Print each command to stderr before executing it.

option.name: -E
tip: If specified, stop processing the input upon reaching an input item that matches eof-string (ignored if -d or -0 is used).

option.name: -I
tip: Replace R in initial arguments with names read from standard input; the input is split at newlines only (mutually exclusive with -L and -n).

option.name: -l
tip: Equivalent to -L, but with a default value of 1 if max-lines is unspecified.
